chief_complaint: Management of non‑small cell lung cancer with associated respiratory symptoms and comorbid chronic conditions
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 48‑year‑old male with early‑stage (TNM stage 1) non‑small cell lung cancer currently receiving adjuvant chemotherapy (paclitaxel and cisplatin). He presents with ongoing respiratory issues including acute bronchitis and a history of viral sinusitis, for which he uses inhaled fluticasone and albuterol. Hypertension is well controlled on lisinopril and amlodipine, but he remains obese (BMI ≥ 30) and has pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.3%). Chronic anemia is noted without recent laboratory confirmation. Psychosocial stressors are prominent: social isolation, limited social contact, and a history of intimate partner abuse. He is employed full‑time, has higher education, and is a military veteran. Recent visits are dominated by inpatient admissions, reflecting complications of cancer therapy and acute infections.

active_problems.name: Non-small cell carcinoma of lung TNM stage 1

past_medical_history: Prior resolved conditions include leaking dental filling, part‑time employment, prior episodes of viral sinusitis and acute viral pharyngitis, gingivitis, and periods of not being in the labor force. These historical issues are no longer active but reflect past dental and respiratory infections.

risk_factor_summary: Clinical complexity is high (Charlson index 1). Hypertension is controlled (BP 111/61) but longstanding. Obesity (BMI missing) and pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.3%) place the patient at elevated metabolic risk. Chronic anemia is present without recent labs. Cancer (stage‑1 NSCLC) and ongoing chemotherapy add oncologic risk. Psychosocial flags (stress, social isolation, intimate partner abuse) increase risk for poor adherence and worse outcomes. Key laboratory gaps: BMI, eGFR, lipid panel, LDL, total cholesterol, and smoking history are missing, limiting full risk stratification.
